articles.title: Jazz Chisholm Jr. Finds Home With Reds Or Nats
articles.summary: Jazz Chisholm Jr. may leave New York. Fox Sports breaks down the best fits for his power and speed, focusing on the Reds and Nationals.
articles.body:
Jazz Chisholm Jr. brings elite speed and power , but his time in New York faces an uncertain future. The Yankees' second baseman posted a career-high 31 home runs in 2025, yet his consistency remains a major question mark. Fox Sports reports that his 1.7 wins above replacement (bWAR) and 97 OPS+ in 2026 likely cost him a long-term deal. Teams will pay for his talent, but they will not commit to a massive contract without proof of stability.

The Washington Nationals offer Chisholm a clear path to rebuild his value. Washington finished third in MLB in runs with 821 and slugged at .423 last season, showing they need more punch up the middle. While Nasim Nuñez led the National League with 49 stolen bases, he lacks the power Chisholm provides. The Nationals could use Chisholm to open 2027 as their starting second baseman and help fill the void left by trading Luis García Jr. and Curtis Mead. Chisholm's move gives him a chance to play either middle infield spot, depending on how the team handles shortstop CJ Abrams.

With only 75 wins, Cincinnati finished last in the National League Central and urgently needs improvement. MLB hits totaled 1,231 for the Reds, who also recorded the league's lowest on-base percentage. Chisholm would give them a capable, impact left-handed hitter to balance the lineup. He would likely start at second base, pushing Matt McLain to the bench. McLain has been the primary second baseman for two years but hit a combined .204 during that stretch. Chisholm's two-time All-Star status would be a massive upgrade for Terry Francona's order.

The market for Chisholm will depend on how teams view his 37.3 stolen bases per season since 2024. He showed he can hit for power, with 80 RBIs in 2025, a year in which he also posted 4.1 wins above replacement. Under Aaron Boone, the Yankees made the postseason eight times over nine years, yet they must determine whether Chisholm belongs in their future. ESPN notes that free agents will come off the board quickly before the league shuts down on Dec. 1.

articles.title: MLB Platinum Gloves Awards 2026 Full List of Winners and Reaction
articles.summary: The New York Yankees' Cody Bellinger and Chicago Cubs' Pete Crow-Armstrong are being celebrated as the best defensive players in MLB.
articles.body:
The New York Yankees' Cody Bellinger and Chicago Cubs' Pete Crow-Armstrong are being celebrated as the best defensive players in MLB.

Bellinger and Armstrong were named 2026 Platinum Glove Award winners the night of the Gold Glove Award Ceremony Friday night in New York City.

Platinum Glove winners are selected from the list of Gold Glove Award winners through combination of fan voting and Society for American Baseball Research (SABR) defensive analytics.

This marks the 16th year in which the award has been distributed since its founding in 2011.

Crow-Armstrong is the first NL center fielder to win a Platinum Glove Award and the second Cubs player since Anthony Rizzo took home the honor in 2011.

He earned the honor after leading the MLB in outs above average (26) and runs prevented (23) while tying for seventh with 16 defensive runs saved, according to Baseball Savant and Fielding Bible .

Crow-Armstrong is also a finalist for the NL MVP award. He could become the first player to win a Platinum Glove and take home an MVP honor in the same season.

Bellinger joins Jose Trevino, who received a Platinum Glove honor in 2022, as the second Yankees player to earn the AL honor.

He recorded six outs above average this season and was credited with preventing six runs and recording 20 defensive runs saved by Baseball Savant and Fielding Bible.

Some fans argued other Gold Glove winners including Boston Red Sox center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela should have been candidates for the honor.

Other Gold Glove Award winners in the AL included Cleveland Guardians pitcher Tanner Bibee, Detroit Tigers catcher Dillon Dingler, Houston Astros first baseman Christian Walker, Seattle Mariners second baseman Cole Young, Boston Red Sox third baseman Caleb Durbin, Tampa Bay Rays shortstop Taylor Walls, Red Sox right fielder Wilyer Abreu and Texas Rangers utility player Ezequiel Duran.

The NL's Gold Glove list was rounded out by New York Mets pitcher Nolan McLean, Arizona Diamondbacks center Gabriel Moreno, Atlanta Braves first baseman Matt Olson, Milwaukee Braves second baseman Brice Turang, Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman, Diamondbacks shortstop Geraldo Perdomo, Brewers left fielder Jackson Chourio, Diamondbacks right field Corbin Carroll and Braves utility player Mauricio Dubón.

Baseball award season will continue over a busy November highlighted by the announcement of All-MLB Teams Nov. 11, and BBWAA MVP awards Nov. 12 and Silver Slugger Awards Nov. 17.

articles.title: MLB announces Pete Crow-Armstrong, Cody Bellinger as Platinum Glove winners in Friday night news dump
articles.summary: Pete Crow-Armstrong and Cody Bellinger were both standouts in the outfield this year.
articles.body:
Pete Crow-Armstrong and Cody Bellinger have won MLB's Platinum Glove awards, meant to honor the top overall defender in each league. It's unclear if the league actually wants people to know that.

For reasons that remain clear only to MLB, the 2026 Platinum Gloves were announced at 11 p.m. ET on Friday, with the Chicago Cubs and New York Yankees taking home an award that is decided by an easily swayed fan vote. It is the first time either player has won the award.

The pair seems happy with their new hardware.

The Platinum Gloves are selected from among the 10 Gold Glovers in each league . This year, those were:

Pitcher: Tanner Bibee , Cleveland Guardians

Catcher: Dillon Dingler , Detroit Tigers

First base: Christian Walker , Houston Astros

Second base: Cole Young , Seattle Mariners

Shortstop: Taylor Walls , Tampa Bay Rays

Third base: Caleb Durbin , Boston Red Sox

Left field: Cody Bellinger , New York Yankees

Center field: Ceddane Rafaela , Boston Red Sox

Right field: Wilyer Abreu , Boston Red Sox

Catcher: Gabriel Moreno , Arizona Diamondbacks

Second base: Brice Turang , Milwaukee Brewers

Shortstop: Geraldo Perdomo , Arizona Diamondbacks

Left field: Jackson Chourio , Milwaukee Brewers

Center field: Pete Crow-Armstrong , Chicago Cubs

Right field: Corbin Carroll , Arizona Diamondbacks

Utility: Mauricio Dubón , Atlanta Braves

The timing of the announcement was nothing new , nor was the methodology. The winner is decided by combining a fan vote held by Rawlings with "votes" from a stat called the SABR Defensive Index (SDI) .

Bellinger led the AL in SDI, while Crow-Armstrong ranked second behind only Milwaukee Brewers second baseman Brice Turang, another Gold Glover. As for other advanced defensive stats, Crow-Armstrong ranked first in his league in Statcast's Fielding Run Value and third in Defensive Runs Saved. Bellinger was 21st and second in those stats, respectively.

It is, of course, extremely difficult to compare defenders across different positions, as these stats are trying to figure out how, say, an outfielder with a penchant for difficult catches compares to a catcher who can throw out runners and frame pitches. It's an inherent flaw of the Platinum Gloves, which would be more of a problem if anyone took them seriously.

At the very least, the Platinum Glove is another feather in the cap this season for Crow-Armstrong, who is widely expected to win NL MVP next week. The Cubs star posted MLB's seventh 40-40 season this year, making him an elite player on offense and defense this season.

Bellinger, meanwhile, received his first All-Star nod since winning NL MVP in 2019 and was among the Yankees' top players this season after returning to the team last winter on a five-year, $162.5 million contract .

Rawling also announced the Toronto Blue Jays and Chicago Cubs as the winners of the Team Gold Gloves. The Cubs ranked third in MLB this season in defensive efficiency (i.e. the rate at which they turned balls in play into outs), while the Blue Jays were 13th. Toronto, which had no Gold Glovers, also led the AL in errors.

articles.title: Buyer Beware on These 8 Potential MLB Free Agent Busts
articles.summary: Teams are caught between a rock and a hard place with this winter's free-agent market. It's a very weak class, yet the time to spend is now before the lockout hits.
articles.body:
Teams are caught between a rock and a hard place with this winter's free-agent market. It's a very weak class, yet the time to spend is now before the lockout hits.

Our advice? Go ahead and spend, but at least know what kind of risk you're taking on with certain players.

There are eight free agents in particular who set off alarm bells, for one reason or another. Some just don't seem especially likely to carry over the success they've had with one team to another. Others have red flags that just can't be ignored.

Let's take a deeper dive into each one of them, going in order of the contracts that B/R's Tim Kelly projected this week.

2026 Stats: 92 G, 14 HR, 1 SB, .256 AVG, .353 OBP, .461 SLG

Ryan Jeffers is a good right-handed hitter at a time when good right-handed hitters are increasingly hard to find . More than that, he's a good right-handed-hitting catcher . He's basically a unicorn.

At the very least, though, teams must understand that Jeffers is more of a warm body behind the plate than a skilled catcher.

His Fielding Run Value for the last four seasons comes out to -24, placing him sixth from the bottom of the list for qualified backstops. He especially struggles to control the running game, which is kind of a problem in today's MLB.

Jeffers' bat was his saving grace this year, yet it comes with the caveat that his -10 Run Value against four-seam fastballs was one of the worst in the league. It was an issue even before he broke his hamate bone in May, as he hit just .229 with a single homer against four-seamers before the injury.

It's not necessarily a bat speed problem, which is the good news. It's nonetheless a weakness that could beexploited more than it was in 2026. Jeffers saw 31.8 percent four-seamers, only a touch above the league average of 30.8.

2026 Stats: 64 G, 69.1 IP, 52 H (4 HR), 76 K, 20 BB, 2.47 ERA

David Bednar got lost in the wilderness in 2024, but he's otherwise been an All-Star-caliber closer for most of the 2020s. He held hitters to a .563 OPS this year, well below his career mark of .623.

The catch is that he lost 7.2 percentage points off his strikeout rate from 2025. That makes it hard to ignore a 0.9 mph drop in his average fastball velocity, as well as a Stuff+ score that went from 108 to 103.

Bednar's adjustment was to double the usage of his splitter, which became a sort of co-go-to pitch with his four-seamer. It worked, specifically in the sense that his chase rate skyrocketed into the 99th percentile.

Yet since Bednar only found the strike zone with 46.0 percent of his pitches, "Don't swing" is now a viable strategy against him. If hitters make that adjustment, his 2026 season could prove to have been built upon a foundation of wet tissue paper.

After all, his splitter carried his repertoire a bit too much this year. It had a +14 Run Value, compared to +2 for his fastball and -1 for his curveball.

2026 Stats: 156 G, 636 PA, 24 HR, 4 SB, .218 AVG, .326 OBP, .412 SLG

Ian Happ is going to hit you between 20 and 25 home runs. He's also going to play a terrific left field. Even if there's no more than this, it's still useful stuff.

However, Happ's Gold Glove-winning defense requires appropriate context. The bar to clear for that position is quite low, and his thing isn't catching fly balls. He has -4 Outs Above Average as a left fielder since 2017.

It's his am that gets the job done, as he's a regular atop the outfield leaderboard for assists. Nothing wrong with that, though he is at an age (32) where it's fair game to worry about wear and tear.

Happ's offense, meanwhile, took an alarming turn toward volatility in 2026. He basically stopped hitting from the right side of the plate, posting a .484 OPS compared to a .816 OPS from the left side. Moreover, his strikeout rate increased by 6.9 percentage points, the third-largest among all hitters.

Hiding in there is trouble with the fastball, as Happ's average against four-seamers has been around or below .200 in three of the last four seasons. This is already something of an open secret for pitchers, so don't expect them to let up as Happ continues to age.

Predicting Most Aggressive Teams in Free Agency 🔮

2026 Stats: 137 G, 532 PA, 19 HR, 41 SB, .231 AVG, .312 OBP, .399 SLG

Pretty much by universal order of decree, there's no avoiding putting Jazz Chisholm Jr. on lists like this. Indeed, he's been boom or bust his whole career.

For a guy who's been a video game cover model and a two-time All-Star, it's surreal that he's topped 4 rWAR just once in seven seasons. That his personality rubs some people the wrong way is a "whatever" thing for the most part, but times when his head doesn't seem to be in the game are harder to forgive.

What really matters right now, of course, is that Chisholm just didn't have a good year in 2026, and least of all at the plate.

It's his .399 slugging percentage that stands out, as it's well below his career mark of .444. It's also hard to wave off. He lost 1 mph in average bat speed from 2025 to 2026, and it mainly manifested in struggles versus heat. Against four-seam fastballs, specifically, he hit .214 with a -10 Run Value.

Chisholm remains a gifted athlete, and that still has value in the field and on the basepaths. Yet this is ultimately a case where a team will have to go all-in on upside, with a very real threat of getting the downside instead.

2026 Teams: New York Mets, Tampa Bay Rays

2026 Stats: 32 GS, 169.0 IP, 161 H (23 HR), 156 K, 63 BB, 4.42 ERA

When he was a Met, you could have said "What a year for Freddy Peralta!" and meant it in a derogatory sense. A 4.99 ERA in 22 starts? That's not great.

His work with the Rays redeemed him, perhaps even more than his results let on. And that's saying something, given that he ended his run in Tampa Bay with a 1.82 ERA in September and October.

Peralta somehow added both to his extension (6.7 feet) and to his fastball velocity (94.8 mph) upon joining the Rays. He also won over FanGraphs' Pitching+ metric, going from a score of 101 as a Met to 110 as a Ray. Only five pitchers did better after the trade deadline.

After all that, his strikeout rate… somehow dropped? Or rather, dropped even further. It got as high as 30.9 percent in 2023. It was 22.1 percent as a Met, and then 19.7 percent as a Ray. Only 11 qualified starters did worse than the latter all year.

It's not an ideal trajectory for a 30-year-old pitcher, and it's not as if substantially better contact quality was his trade-off at the end of the year. So even if he does carry over what worked as a Ray, sustainability will be a question.

2026 Stats: 150 G, 656 PA, 35 HR, 2 SB, .260 AVG, .331 OBP, .493 SLG

Brandon Lowe picked a heck of a year to post a career-best 5.3 rWAR, and we'd be remiss if we didn't acknowledge how big of a role his defense played.

Before 2026, Lowe was known as a bad defensive second baseman. Not so this year, including to the tune of a +29 swing in Outs Above Average. All it took was the right coaching , so we'll roll with it as something that could be sustainable.

Otherwise, two of this three 30-homer seasons have come in the last two years. He had his best year ever for pulling the ball in the air , which is still another revolution that passes the smell test.

The bad stuff concerns what happened when Lowe didn't make contact. His 28.8 K% marked his highest strikeout rate since 2019, and it might undersell how much he swung and missed. He had a 66.9 contact percentage, third-lowest among qualified hitters.

That would be easy to forgive if Lowe had good plate discipline, but his 33.6 chase percentage was a career high and in the 27th percentile to boot. That's never ideal, and least of all for a 32-year-old whose "old man skills" should be getting sharper.

2026 Stats: 30 GS, 169.2 IP, 162 H (19 HR), 157 K, 39 BB, 4.03 ERA

A 2.64 ERA over 25 starts made Trevor Rogers an All-Star and Rookie of the Year contender in 2021. In 2025, he made 18 starts and pitched to a 1.81 ERA. This year, he had a 6.84 ERA at the end of May before ripping off a 2.90 ERA in his last 20 starts.

There's a difference between a good run and a good season, however, and Rogers has yet to prove he can handle the latter. That is, at least if you consider a good season from a starter to consist of 30-plus starts' worth of consistency.

Optimistically, his free agency is a chance to get in on the ground floor of a late-blooming ace, a la Zack Wheeler in 2019. There is support for the idea, including how Pitching+ rated Rogers (106) higher than Paul Skenes (105) this year.

Even setting aside the inconsistency, though, there's still a broader lack of swing-and-miss stuff (46th percentile Whiff% this year) and one heck of a platoon disadvantage. Righties had a .759 OPS against Rogers this year, compared to a .515 OPS for lefties.

Normally, a good changeup can solve a problem like that. But the change is already Rogers' primary offering, and righties hit .338 with a .303 xBA against it this season. Per its -11 Run Value, it was the worst changeup in baseball.

2026 Stats: 32 GS, 185.0 IP, 148 H (20 HR), 159 K, 70 BB, 3.21 ERA

This is just no fun at all, precisely because watching Michael King pitch is all sorts of fun. The movement on his stuff is devilish in the best way, and there just aren't many who can work the east-west sides of the plate like he can.

However, seen his Baseball Savant page lately? It's shockingly not impressive.

He was average or worse for a bunch of key indicators this year, most notably including a strikeout rate that fell into the 38th percentile. His walk rate wasn't much better, landing in the 40th percentile. Overall, he had the sixth-lowest Pitching+ score among qualified starters.

It was his capacity for limiting hard contact (i.e., hard-hit rate in the 89th percentile) that sustained him, but some of the credit goes to the defenders he had behind him in San Diego. Per Outs Above Average , no pitcher benefited more from his defense this season.

The best thing for King, then, might be to re-up with the Padres. With any other team, he'll be at risk.

Stats courtesy of Baseball Reference , FanGraphs and Baseball Savant .

articles.title: More zeroes for Cody Morse in the Arizona Fall League
articles.summary: Runs were hard to come by for the Glendale Desert Dogs on Friday night in a 1-0 road loss to the Scottsdale Scorpions in the Arizona Fall League. Glendale on...
articles.body:
Runs were hard to come by for the Glendale Desert Dogs on Friday night in a 1-0 road loss to the Scottsdale Scorpions in the Arizona Fall League. Glendale only had five hits, all singles, and Dodgers prospects accounted for three of the five hits.

Third baseman Chase Harlan had two hits, while second baseman Charles Davalan had a single and walked, but that wasn't enough for the Desert Dogs to touch home plate.

Cody Morse inherited runners on first and second base with two outs in the sixth inning, and stranded them with a groundout. Then Morse added a scoreless seventh, with one walk and a strikeout. The left-hander has been nearly spotless in his nine appearances so far in the Arizona Fall League, allowing only one unearned run on two hits and five walks in eight innings. To go with that 0.00 ERA, Morse has 14 strikeouts among his 33 batters faced for a tidy 42.4-percent strikeout rate.

Sam Horn, the Missouri quarterback turned Dodgers minor league pitcher, did not pitch Friday, but in his professional debut in the AFL has a 3.86 ERA in seven innings with eight strikeouts and four walks in his seven games. Horn was among the 10 pitchers in Arizona profiled by Geoff Pontes at Baseball America .

"He mixes three pitches: a mid-90s four-seam fastball with seven feet of extension, an 83-85 mph sweeper and a firm upper-80s changeup with negative vertical break." Pontes wrote . "Horn has a limited track record, but he's an exciting upside play."

articles.title: What made the Shohei Ohtani and Ippei Mizuhara gambling scandal so shocking: How the investigation reshaped the Los Angeles Dodgers star’s reputation and MLB legacy
articles.summary: Explore the shocking gambling scandal involving Shohei Ohtani and Ippei Mizuhara, revealing how financial fraud reshaped the MLB star's reputation and the challenges faced by professional athletes regarding trust and financial oversight.
articles.body: Shohei Ohtani’s extraordinary achievements on the baseball field have made him one of the most recognisable athletes in the world. He went to the Los Angeles Dodgers in 2023, signed a record contract, and the expectations grew, and the spotlight became intense; but in March 2024, the attention turned away from his play to a gambling scandal involving his longtime interpreter and close friend, Ippei Mizuhara.The revelations raised questions that extended far beyond sports betting. Mizuhara had been part of Ohtani’s professional life for years, helping him communicate, manage everyday responsibilities and navigate life in the United States. When reports emerged that millions of dollars had been transferred from Ohtani’s bank account to cover gambling debts, the baseball world wanted to know what had happened and whether the Dodgers superstar had been involved. The subsequent investigation established that Ohtani was the victim of an extensive financial fraud, while Mizuhara admitted to stealing from him.Shohei Ohtani and Ippei Mizuhara gambling scandal explainedThe scandal became public in March 2024, when reports connected Mizuhara to an illegal sports betting operation in California. The central issue was whether Ohtani had knowingly provided money to cover Mizuhara’s gambling debts or whether his account had been accessed without his permission.Mizuhara had worked closely with Ohtani since the player's arrival in Major League Baseball in 2018. As his interpreter, he accompanied him through interviews, team activities, travel and other professional commitments. Their frequent public appearances created the impression of a close working relationship built on trust. That made the allegations particularly startling: the person entrusted with helping Ohtani manage life in a different country was accused of exploiting that position for personal financial gain.Federal investigators later established that Mizuhara had stolen nearly $17 million from Ohtani’s bank account. The money was used to pay gambling debts and support his betting activity. Investigators also found that Mizuhara had impersonated Ohtani when communicating with the bank, helping him gain access to the player's funds without his knowledge or authorisation.How Ippei Mizuhara’s theft affected Shohei OhtaniThe most immediate impact on Ohtani was the sudden loss of trust in someone who had been a central figure in his professional life. An interpreter in Major League Baseball does more than translate words. The role can involve helping a player communicate with coaches, teammates, reporters and officials, particularly when the player is still developing confidence in a new language and environment.The early reporting also created uncertainty around Ohtani’s role. The first explanations surrounding the transfers were disputed, and the story developed rapidly as new details emerged. Ohtani’s representatives denied that he had knowingly paid Mizuhara’s gambling debts. Federal investigators later supported the position that the player had been defrauded, identifying him as the victim rather than a participant in the betting activity.That distinction was essential to the way the scandal was understood. Ohtani was not charged with a crime, and the investigation did not establish that he had placed bets or knowingly funded Mizuhara’s gambling. Instead, the evidence showed that Mizuhara had used unauthorised access and deception to take money from the baseball star.The case also raised broader questions about the safeguards surrounding professional athletes’ finances. Players who move internationally can rely on interpreters, agents and other trusted representatives to handle important daily responsibilities. While those relationships can be essential, the Ohtani case demonstrated how vulnerable a person can become when financial access and personal trust are concentrated in one individual.For the Dodgers, the scandal created an unexpected distraction at the beginning of Ohtani’s first season with the organisation. The club had signed him as a transformative player, but the opening weeks of the 2024 campaign became associated with an investigation that attracted international attention. The team and the player had to navigate questions about the case while continuing the regular demands of a Major League Baseball season.How Shohei Ohtani returned focus to Dodgers baseballOnce federal investigators clarified the nature of Mizuhara’s actions, attention gradually returned to Ohtani’s performances. The findings removed the central suspicion surrounding the player and allowed the baseball conversation to focus on his contribution to the Dodgers. His response on the field became a significant part of the story, particularly because he was entering a new chapter with a team expected to compete for a championship.That made the feat even more impressive considering it was his first year with the Dodgers and first season primarily as a designated hitter while recovering from elbow surgery. Although he did not pitch during the season, his offensive production demonstrated that he could remain an elite player while following a different role on the field.What the scandal changed for MLB and its playersThe case also became an important moment for conversations about gambling, financial security and the responsibilities of people working closely with professional athletes. MLB has strict rules governing gambling by players and club personnel, particularly when betting involves baseball. The Ohtani investigation, however, was not a case of the star violating those rules. It centred on an interpreter's illegal betting activity and the theft of a player's money.That distinction was important to the league’s reputation and to the public’s perception of the case. The investigation showed why allegations connected with gambling should be examined closely, and not be taken as proof of a player's participation. It also highlighted the need for solid evidence when a high-profile athlete’s name becomes tied to a criminal investigation through a member of his personal or professional world.It was a case in point for the players that trust and financial oversight are two different things. Long-term professional relationships are no substitute for secure banking practices, independent financial advice and clear limits on who can access personal accounts. The scandal revealed how the power of a single person over day-to-day arrangements can open the door to serious abuse where safeguards are lacking.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: A government witness admitted to winning thousands betting on Emmanuel Clase's pitch speeds using inside tips shared through an Uber driver group chat.
articles.body: As the Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz federal trial continued on Friday in New York, a government witness added a very interesting wrinkle to the case during his testimony. Luis de Aza Baez admitted to placing dozens of bets, and winning thousands, by wagering on the speed Clase’s pitch came across home plate during the 2023 MLB season. He said he placed the bets "because I had inside information," per ESPN. Clase has been accused of rigging 18 pitches across three seasons in conspiracy with bettors. "What was going on with [Shohei] Ohtani, there was no more information like that," de Aza Baez said in his testimony. In March 2024, Ohtani wasn’t facing accusations like Clase and Ortiz, but he faced scrutiny after millions had been sent from his bank account to an illegal bookmaking operation. But Ippei Mizuhara, his longtime interpreter, pleaded guilty to stealing almost $17 million from Ohtani to pay off gambling debts. MLB CATCHER WHO WAS BEHIND PLATE FOR ALLEGED RIGGED PITCHES TESTIFIES IN GUARDIANS PITCHERS' GAMBLING CASE Mizuhara is currently in prison, while Ohtani was cleared of any wrongdoing in the case. De Aza Baez was working as an Uber driver at the time, and he had a group chat called "Uber Inc.," where Enoc Pena, an associate of Clase, would send tips in 2023, according to his testimony. Pena was the one who started the chat with the men who worked for Uber in the Massachusetts area. Prosecutors showed a text message screenshot Clase allegedly had sent to Pena on Sept. 30, 2023, when the Cleveland Guardians were set to face the Detroit Tigers. Clase and Pena spoke about "killing the first two chickens," which was code to bet on a pitch against the third batter, granted Clase came in the game and got the first two outs. He never entered the contest in the 8-0 Detroit victory. Clase’s defense team argued the text message was misconstrued, as roosters and chickens in such talks with Pena often refer to cockfighting, which is legal in his native Dominican Republic. De Aza Baez and Clase became friends, and were seen in a video at a relative’s house playing dominoes on a Boston Red Sox-logoed table. However, de Aza Baez testified he never received direct information about pitches from Clase – only Pena. De Aza Baez said he "almost always" won when Pena dropped the tip to him, and though there were no official cuts to be handed out, he gave him some money after winning the bet. Clase and Ortiz, also an ex-Guardians pitcher have pleaded not guilty to conspiracy of wire and honor services fraud, sports bribery and money laundering. "Our defense is the same today as it was in opening: This is a case about big talk and small bets," Vásquez's attorney Todd Spodek told ESPN following the hearing on Friday. "We're confident leaving that judgment to the jury." De Aza Baez agreed with the federal government to forfeit $69,000 won on bets involving Clase, saying he would "tell the truth" in exchange for dropping the wire fraud charge in the case. Prior to De Aza Baez’s testimony, former Guardians catcher Bo Naylor, who was behind the plate for the allegedly rigged pitches by both Clase and Ortiz, testified on Thursday in New York. He said he appeared to call one of the allegedly rigged pitches that were shown to him on a screen inside the courtroom, saying that a slider away to St. Louis Cardinals’ Pedro Pages was a weakness. He also noted he was unaware bettors could even wager on specific pitches. Attorneys elicited from Naylor that he had frequently seen Clase on his cellular phone in the locker room. articles.body:
Major League Baseball confirmed Saturday that right-handed relief pitcher Jyun-Yue Tseng, who has played all six of his professional seasons for the Fubon Guardians of the Chinese Professional Baseball League in Taiwan, is entering the posting system.

The Associated Press reported the news earlier Saturday.

Predicting Most Aggressive Teams in Free Agency 🔮

The 25-year-old is eligible to sign with an MLB team as a free agent any time from Sunday through Dec. 22. However, the current collective bargaining agreement expires on Dec. 1, and MLB can lock out the Major League Baseball Players Association, which would slice that negotiating period by three weeks, as the AP noted.

Tseng made 48 appearances last year, striking out 65 and walking just 13 over 52.1 innings while amassing 25 saves, per the AP.

Dustin Riese of CubsHQ added that Tseng's fastball can reach up to 97 mph. He also noted Tseng had a near-33 percent strikeout rate and a near-31 percent whiff rate.

As far as potential landing spots are concerned, reports indicate that the Chicago Cubs, Pittsburgh Pirates and Los Angeles Dodgers have shown varying levels of interest.

Brett Taylor of Bleacher Nation provided more insight on Tseng from the Cubs' perspective.

"It maybe more of a developmental play at a lower price if the Cubs were to go after Tseng, rather than a sure-fire impact move in the bullpen. From clips I've seen, Tseng throws a slider, a splitter, and a fastball that touches 97.5 mph, which wouldn't be elite, but very easily could be playable if it comes with other compelling pitch characteristics."

Tseng, listed at 5'8" and 150 pounds, also appeared in this year's World Baseball Classic for Chinese Taipei and registered a pair of scoreless innings over two appearances, striking out two. That included a huge save to cap a massive upset for Chinese Taipei over Korea, 5-4 in 10 innings.

Now Tseng will try his hand in the major leagues after a great 2026 season.

articles.title: Reggie Jackson calls out antisemitism in native Pennsylvania, likens it to 'racism I experienced in the 1960s'
articles.summary: Baseball Hall of Famer Reggie Jackson compared rising antisemitism in Pennsylvania to the racism he endured in the 1960s South as a Black player.
articles.body: Baseball Hall of Famer Reggie Jackson called out antisemitism on social media and said it is comparable to the "racism I received in the 1960s." On Saturday morning, Mr. October posted a link to the Anti-Defamation League’s website and cited statistics showing an increase in antisemitic incidents across Pennsylvania, his native state. Jackson was born in Wyncote, near Philadelphia. "It takes me back to the racism I experienced in the 1960s: signs throughout the South declaring that Black people could be refused service, along with separate 'white' and 'colored' signs on bathrooms and drinking fountains, 'no n—s.' I remember what that hatred looked and felt like. We cannot accept it in any form, directed at any people," Jackson wrote. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Jackson then called out politicians and leaders in the Philadelphia area. "I wish I could be there to stand with those protesting HATE. I am asking elected officials and other leaders in Philadelphia: Where are the clear statements condemning antisemitism? When hateful language is excused or repeated, it can make hostility seem acceptable and deepen fear and division. Leaders should speak plainly and consistently: antisemitism and hate have no place in our communities. What the hell? We have to speak up," he said. Jackson unearthed the racism he experienced when MLB made its inaugural trip to Rickwood Field in Birmingham, Alabama in 2024 as a nod to the Negro Leagues. MLB CATCHER WHO WAS BEHIND PLATE FOR ALLEGED RIGGED PITCHES TESTIFIES IN GUARDIANS PITCHERS' GAMBLING CASE "The racism when I played here, the difficulty of going through different places where we traveled … I wouldn’t wish it on anybody," Jackson began before sharing his harsh reality of playing for the Birmingham Black Barons, which were a minor league affiliate of the then Kansas City Athletics. "I would walk into restaurants, they would point at me and say ‘that n----- can’t eat here.’ I would go to a hotel, and they’d say ‘that n----- can’t stay here.’ We went to [former A's owner] Charlie Finley’s country club for a welcome-home dinner, and they pointed me out with the n-word, ‘he can’t come in here …' "Had it not been for Rollie Fingers, Johnny McNamara, Dave Duncan, Joe and Sharron Rudy, I slept on their couch three or four nights a week for about a month and a half. Finally, they threatened to burn our apartment complex down unless I got out. I wouldn’t wish it on anybody." articles.title: New Top 100 MLB Prospect Rankings for 2026-27 Offseason
articles.summary: With the MLB offseason officially underway, the Bleacher Report Top 100 prospect list deserves an update to account for the players who exhausted their prospect status down the stretch, others who thrived as September call-ups and even a few Arizona Fall League standouts.
articles.body:
With the MLB offseason officially underway, the Bleacher Report Top 100 prospect list deserves an update to account for the players who exhausted their prospect status down the stretch, others who thrived as September call-ups and even a few Arizona Fall League standouts.

The following factors helped determine where each player fell in our rankings:

Future Potential: Long-term upside often trumps production in prospect discussions, especially in the lower levels of the minors and with recent draft picks. Raw tools often better indicate future value than early on-field production.

Present Tools: For prospects in the upper levels of the minors who are close to reaching the big leagues, on-field production and polished tools were the deciding factors, as those players are viewed as more complete products.

Eligibility: A player must maintain rookie eligibility to be considered for inclusion. That means no more than 130 big-league at-bats for position players, 50 innings for pitchers or 45 days on the active roster.

After a terrific stateside debut, Hayden Alvarez emerged as one of the top prospects in the Angels system in 2026, hitting .289/.391/.456 with 32 doubles, 12 home runs and 53 steals in 118 games between Single-A and High-A. The 19-year-old also has significant physical projection remaining in his 6'3", 190-pound frame.

A switch-hitting middle infielder with a quality hit tool and plus athleticism, Welbyn Francisca fits the type of player the Guardians have done a nice job developing in recent years. He posted an .879 OPS over 79 games while reaching Double-A in his age-20 season, and currently has a gaudy .419/.482/.716 line with 12 extra-base hits over 85 plate appearances in the Arizona Fall League.

One of the top power bats in the 2025 draft class, Xavier Neyens posted an .874 OPS with 20 home runs in 103 games between Single-A and High-A in his pro debut. A 33.3 percent strikeout rate raises some red flags, but it was accompanied by 114 walks and a 24.5 percent walk rate.

In 77 games between Single-A and High-A, he batted .282/.417/.546 with 19 home runs and 33 steals, and he is making up for lost time in the Arizona Fall League.

Widely regarded as the best defensive catcher in the 2026 draft class, Ryder Helfrick also slugged 33 home runs in 123 games during his final two seasons at Arkansas. He jumped straight to Single-A for his pro debut, and posted an .849 OPS with seven doubles, five home runs and 17 RBI in 24 games.

Cam Cannarella already looks like one of the steals of the 2025 draft class, when he was taken No. 43 overall by the Marlins. Tate Southisene looked like a bit of a reach at No. 21 overall in the 2025 MLB draft, but he quickly erased any second-guessing when he posted a .278/.408/.467 line with 35 extra-base hits and 45 steals in 90 games while reaching Double-A in his first full professional campaign.

Despite an undersized 5'9" frame, Charles Davalan has quickly proven to have one of the best combinations of hit tool and raw power in a deep Dodgers farm system since going No. 41 overall in the 2025 draft. With George Lombard Jr. officially graduating to the majors, Dax Kilby now stands as the consensus top prospect in the Yankees system. The No. 7 overall pick and consensus best overall athlete in the 2026 draft class, Eric Booth Jr. has the tools and upside to fly up these rankings in 2027. The Baseball America 2026 Minor League Player of the Year, slugger Andrew Fischer posted a 1.066 OPS with 48 home runs and 114 RBI in 126 games between High-A and Double-A. With Brooks Lee shifting to third base, Kaelen Culpepper got an extended look at Minnesota's starting shortstop after making his MLB debut on Aug. 7. He hit .274/.328/.393 for a 102 OPS+ over 128 plate appearances and played solid defense ( -1 DRS, 1 OAA ), giving him the inside track to win the Opening Day job in 2027.

Part of a loaded 2024 draft class, Seaver King was taken No. 10 overall out of Vanderbilt, and he is one of only two top-10 picks who has yet to make his MLB debut. After hitting .303/.382/.516 with 24 doubles, 21 home runs and 74 RBI in 112 games between Double-A and Triple-A, that call could come early in 2027.

Caden Bodine showcased some of the best bat-to-ball skills of any prospect in his first season in the Tampa Bay organization after coming over in the Shane Baz trade with Baltimore. He hit .342/.410/.517 with 17 home runs and 99 RBI, and put the ball in play in over 80 percent of his plate appearances.

With a strong 6'2", 210-pound frame and some of the best raw power in the minors, Alfredo Duno looks like the catcher of the not-too-distant future in Cincinnati. The Tigers acquired Zyhir Hope at the trade deadline in the Tarik Skubal blockbuster, and he should join Riley Greene and Max Clark in the Detroit outfield at some point in 2027. Still only 21 years old, he hit .287/.367/.513 with 29 home runs, 111 RBI and 26 steals in 124 games at Double-A.

One of the biggest breakout prospects of 2026, outfielder Josiah Hartshorn went from handsomely-paid sixth-round pick in the 2025 draft to the consensus top prospect in the Cubs farm system. articles.title: Voting on MLB's 2026 Awards for AL and NL MVP, Cy Young, Rookie of the Year, More
articles.summary: Before we can officially close the book on Major League Baseball's 2026 season, one key hurdle remains: Awards Week.
articles.body:
Before we can officially close the book on Major League Baseball's 2026 season, one key hurdle remains: Awards Week.

Gold Gloves have already been handed out, but the Rookie of the Year announcements will come on Monday night. Manager of the Year follows on Tuesday. Cy Young and Reliever of the Year Awards will be announced on Wednesday. And then the MVP ceremonies take place on Thursday.

For each of those 10 awards (five per league), we know the three finalists. And, for the most part, we can already say with 99 percent (or more) confidence who the winner will be.

But let's address them all, in chronological order.

The Three Finalists (announcement on Nov. 9)

Kevin McGonigle, Detroit Tigers (.278/.376/.430, 18 HR, 72 RBI, 12 SB, 7.1 bWAR )

Parker Messick, Cleveland Guardians (186.1 IP, 2.56 ERA, 3.07 FIP, 1.06 WHIP, 9.3 K/9, 6.3 bWAR )

Payton Tolle, Boston Red Sox (148.2 IP, 3.03 ERA, 3.04 FIP, 1.10 WHIP, 10.4 K/9, 2.9 bWAR )

If I didn't know the betting odds where McGonigle is the massive favorite, or if I didn't know that McGonigle basically had this race wrapped up by the All-Star Break, I would expect this one to be a photo finish between the Tigers infielder and the Guardians ace, if not a clear victory for Messick.

(Unless this year's voters filled out their ballots based upon who they would most want to just hang out with for a day, in which case Tolle wins in unanimous fashion.)

Please don't misconstrue any of this as McGonigle slander. He is a special young talent who played basically every day, posting one of the best on-base percentages in the majors while oscillating between two demanding positions on defense. He is a deserving Rookie of the Year.

But Messick became just the sixth rookie pitcher in the past 50 years to log at least 170 innings with an ERA of 2.67 or better. The five who preceded him on that list were Fernando Valenzuela (1981), Orel Hershisher (1984), Dwight Gooden (1984), Hideo Nomo (1995) and José Fernández (2013).

In other words, it hadn't been done in more than a decade, it has now been done just twice in the past three decades and it has only been accomplished in the past half-century by instant sensations.

Moreover, Messick was the most important player on a team that wouldn't have made the postseason without him, while McGonigle was stellar for an 86-loss Tigers team this year.

I know we've evolved beyond the days of handing MVP awards to the player who had the most RBI on the team that won the most games, but shouldn't team success matter at least to some extent? That the Guardians needed Messick in a tight playoff race and that they went 18-3 when scoring at least three runs in games where he was the starter?

McGonigle is going to win, possibly in unanimous fashion. But the fact that Messick is also one of three finalists for AL Cy Young speaks volumes to how impressive he was.

Carson Benge, New York Mets (.282/.346/.430, 20 HR, 65 RBI, 22 SB, 4.3 bWAR )

Sal Stewart, Cincinnati Reds (.263/.330/.457, 32 HR, 112 RBI, 15 SB, 1.8 bWAR )

JJ Wetherholt, St. Louis Cardinals (.242/.339/.365, 17 HR, 51 RBI, 14 SB, 4.5 bWAR )

For as much as we talk about Wins Above Replacement on a daily basis, you would think that Stewart has no chance whatsoever of winning this one.

Gold Glove finalists Benge and Wetherholt smoked the Silver Slugger finalist in the WAR department, both per Baseball-Reference and per FanGraphs .

What's more, Benge did so with an OPS+ of 118 that actually bested Stewart's mark of 117. Wetherholt was no slouch at the dish, either, with 17 home runs. It's not like we're comparing light-hitting defensive phenoms Ozzie Smith and Omar Vizquel to David Ortiz here.

Stewart repeatedly delivered in big moments, though, and that narrative kind of outweighed everything else in the end.

While Benge had a .652 OPS with runners in scoring position and Wetherholt had a .639 OPS in high-leverage situations, Stewart's marks were .924 and .976, respectively, as he almost became the first rookie to lead the majors in RBI since Walt Dropo in 1950.

Unlike the AL ROY conversation, team success couldn't possibly factor into this vote, as the Cardinals, Reds and Mets suffered 85, 87 and 88 losses, respectively. But Stewart was probably one of the most clutch players to ever play for an 87-loss team.

The Three Finalists (announcement on Nov. 10)

Chad Tracy, Boston Red Sox (87-75; 77-58 after he took over)

Quite the variety of options here, each of whom presents a compelling case.

Tracy inherited a 10-17 mess when Boston fired Alex Cora, but he turned it into a No. 5 seed. He did so despite Garrett Crochet not making a single regular season appearance while Tracy was the manager and despite losing Roman Anthony for nearly four months. That 32-5 run the Red Sox went on from late June into early August was legendary.

Cash's Rays were the biggest overachiever in all of baseball, at least as far as preseason win totals are concerned. They were 'supposed' to win 76.5 games, but they actually won 98, securing the AL's No. 1 seed with room to spare. In any normal year, he'd be the easy pick.

Venable's White Sox made history, though, and emphatically so.

Not only did they become the first team to win at least 71 games in a season immediately after three consecutive years of at least 100 losses, but the White Sox got to 84 wins and a spot in the postseason that simply no one had forecasted headed into the season, even in an AL Central that was expected to be wide open for the taking.

If they had actually won the division and secured a first-round bye, this would be even more of a no-brainer selection. As is, though, it'd be a bit of a shocker if Venable doesn't win it.

Don Mattingly, Philadelphia Phillies (88-74; 79-55 after he took over)

Early in the season, this looked like Weiss' trophy to lose. Not only did the Braves have the best record in all of baseball in early June (45-21; three games ahead of the Dodgers) but they were doing so with a new manager, fresh off a disappointing 76-86 end to Brian Snitker's tenure.

From that point forward, however, the Braves were the textbook definition of average (49-47, zero run differential) while Mattingly led the Phillies back from their early grave and Murphy steered the Brewers to new heights yet again.

What Mattingly did—posting a .590 winning percentage en route to the postseason after taking over a team with a .321 winning percentage—was remarkable stuff.

He merely brought the Phillies back to the level of competence that they were supposed to be at all along, though, with a fair amount of thanks due to Zack Wheeler, who made his season debut in late April before likely pitching his way to a Comeback Player of the Year award.

Meanwhile, Murphy led the Brewers to an MLB-best (and franchise-best) 103 wins. He did so with a team that not only had a middling payroll, but got very little from the two players on the roster who did have an eight-figure cash salary—Christian Yelich and Brandon Woodruff.

Even though he has already won this award in each of the past two seasons, it almost has to go to Murphy yet again.

The Three Finalists (announcement on Nov. 11)

Dylan Cease, Toronto Blue Jays (169.0 IP, 2.40 ERA, 2.56 FIP, 1.10 WHIP, 12.7 K/9, 5.5 bWAR )

Cam Schlittler, New York Yankees (193.2 IP, 1.95 ERA, 2.56 FIP, 0.92 WHIP, 11.1 K/9, 7.0 bWAR )

This was one heck of a race between Schlittler and Cease for several months.

On Aug. 6, Cease tossed seven shutout innings against the Cubs, lowering his ERA to 2.28. Three days later, Schlittler allowed a solo home run in seven otherwise masterful innings against the Braves, lowering his ERA to 2.21.

At that point, it truly could have gone either way.

But while Cease somewhat limped to the finish line before missing his final start with shoulder inflammation, Schlittler only got stronger, posting a 1.15 ERA across his final eight starts.

As a result, he ended up with the eighth season in the past 30 years of at least 190 innings pitched with both a sub-2.00 ERA and sub-1.00 WHIP.

Of the other seven members of that club—Jacob deGrom in 2018, Jake Arrieta and Zack Greinke in 2015, Clayton Kershaw in 2013 and 2014, Pedro Martínez in 1997 and 2000—five won the Cy Young in landslide fashion, while Arrieta and Greinke basically split the NL vote in 2015.

Expect another landslide victor here, as Schlittler ran away with it down the stretch.

Jacob Misiorowski, Milwaukee Brewers (174.2 IP, 1.80 ERA, 2.17 FIP, 0.80 WHIP, 13.0 K/9, 6.5 bWAR )

Chris Sale, Atlanta Braves (162.2 IP, 2.16 ERA, 2.29 FIP, 0.98 WHIP, 11.1 K/9, 5.5 bWAR )

Cristopher Sánchez, Philadelphia Phillies (207.0 IP, 2.91 ERA, 2.80 FIP, 1.20 WHIP, 10.0 K/9, 8.1 bWAR )

Sánchez had a fantastic season, featuring an historic stretch of 50.2 consecutive scoreless innings pitched. For the second consecutive year, he ended up with an 8.1 bWAR that led all pitchers . (Certainly one of the better two-year runs we've ever seen from a starting pitcher, even though it's going to result in zero Cy Young awards.)

Sale was also marvelous, reaching 200 strikeouts in spite of Atlanta consistently giving its 37-year-old ace extra rest en route to just 27 starts. Among qualified pitchers, he led the majors in both K/BB ratio (6.45) and home run rate (0.55 per nine innings pitched).

But, you know, thanks for playing, southpaws, as the flame-throwing Misiorowski is likely to win this one in unanimous fashion.

Pretty much every baseball fan agrees that Pedro Martínez's 2000 campaign was one of the five greatest seasons of all-time. He had a 1.74 ERA, 0.74 WHIP and an 11.8 K/9. It was (until this season) one of just two cases in MLB history of at least 160 innings pitched with a sub-2.00 ERA and a sub-0.90 WHIP. (The other came in Clayton Kershaw's MVP and Cy Young season in 2014.)

Misiorowski's numbers ended up almost identical to Martínez's, albeit in 42.1 fewer innings pitched.

The velocity is what made every single one of his starts go viral. But it was the dominant efficiency that made this one of the most impressive seasons ever.

Bryan Baker, Tampa Bay Rays (41 saves, 62.1 IP, 1.44 ERA, 3.07 FIP, 0.91 WHIP, 9.1 K/9, 2.9 bWAR )

Cade Smith, Cleveland Guardians (41 saves, 74.0 IP, 1.95 ERA, 2.18 FIP, 0.96 WHIP, 13.0 K/9, 2.9 bWAR )

Louis Varland, Toronto Blue Jays (35 saves, 78.0 IP, 1.27 ERA, 1.83 FIP, 1.00 WHIP, 11.2 K/9, 3.6 bWAR )

Before we try to project a winner in this biggest toss-up of the 10 awards, could we just marvel for a moment at the sheer unexpectedness of two of the three players on this list?

Baker entered 2026 with a career 3.86 ERA and just four saves. Last July, the Orioles traded him to the Rays for a draft pick, fresh off a disastrous "four batters faced, four earned runs allowed" performance in a loss. He ended up blowing six saves that season, despite pitching in just 22 save/hold situations.

Varland's ascension to dominance was even more improbable, entering this season with a 4.66 ERA and nary a save in his career. The Blue Jays turned to him in darn near every game during their 2025 postseason run, but he was never expected to become their closer.

Throw Texas' Jacob Latz in there, too, as the unofficial No. 4 pitcher on this list. The only save he had prior to this season was one of those "pitched the final three innings of a blowout" situations, but he also became an All-Star closer out of nowhere.

Even Smith only became a closer last season because of Emmanuel Clase's expulsion from MLB, and he merely went 13-for-17 in save situations with a 2.79 ERA after inheriting the job.

Without further ado, though, we'll go with Baker. Because while Varland had arguably the most dominant season of the bunch, Baker was the impenetrable force for the American League's best squad.

He had a few blown saves early in the year, all three coming in situations where he entered in the eighth inning. He converted each of his final 30 save chances, though, with a 0.82 ERA from May 17 onward. (Not even including his postseason run of 10 scoreless innings with two hits allowed.)

Jhoan Duran, Philadelphia Phillies (33 saves, 59.1 IP, 1.82 ERA, 1.41 FIP, 0.99 WHIP, 12.7 K/9, 3.4 bWAR )

Trevor Megill, Milwaukee Brewers (30 saves, 61.2 IP, 2.63 ERA, 1.85 FIP, 0.89 WHIP, 10.1 K/9, 1.8 bWAR )

Mason Miller, San Diego Padres (38 saves, 70.0 IP, 1.67 ERA, 1.17 FIP, 0.90 WHIP, 16.6 K/9, 3.1 bWAR )

Had the season ended on August 24, Mason Miller would've had an almost indisputable case for the most dominant season by a reliever in MLB history.

To that point, he had a 0.81 ERA and a 0.64 FIP, striking out 48.1 percent of batters faced without allowing a single home run. And among the more than 28,000 seasons of at least 50 innings pitched, there has never been a FIP lower than 0.78.

Despite allowing three home runs and a 4.91 ERA the rest of the way, Miller still ended up with the fifth-lowest FIP in a season of at least 50 innings pitched in MLB history.

Basically, there's a reason pretty much everyone rushed to assume he must have been tipping his pitches during his disappointing showing in Game 2 of the NLDS against Milwaukee.

Megill and especially Duran had excellent seasons in their own right, but this one isn't going to be close.

The Three Finalists (announcement on Nov. 12)

Yordan Alvarez, Houston Astros (.316/.432/.601, 42 HR, 106 RBI, 6.8 bWAR )

Junior Caminero, Tampa Bay Rays (.276/.360/.524, 42 HR, 101 RBI, 5.7 bWAR )

Bobby Witt Jr., Kansas City Royals (.281/.359/.441, 18 HR, 54 RBI, 45 SB, 6.7 bWAR )

Dating back to Y2K, there have been four instances in which a player led the majors in batting average, on-base percentage and slugging percentage.

Barry Bonds did so in 2002, winning NL MVP unanimously.

Miguel Cabrera did it in 2013, winning AL MVP not quite unanimously, but by a wide margin.

Aaron Judge did it last year, edging out Cal Raleigh's historic 60-homer campaign for AL MVP.

And Yordan Alvarez did it this season, and will be named AL MVP for it.

He fell a bit shy of the Triple Crown goal, sputtering a bit over the final two months and finishing one home run and seven RBI behind Baltimore's Pete Alonso. But he was such a force of nature through the first four months—finishing July with a 1.077 OPS, on pace for 52 home runs and 122 RBI—that he pretty much just needed to stay healthy through August and September in order to secure this hardware.

Caminero did his best to keep things interesting, though. He ended up with the same number of home runs and very similar totals in the runs and RBI departments while actually playing defense on a daily basis—granted, not good defense—for a Rays team that won 17 more games than the Astros.

Maybe someone throws him a first-place vote to keep Alvarez from winning unanimously.

Pete Crow-Armstrong, Chicago Cubs (.280/.372/.570, 45 HR, 107 RBI, 41 SB, 9.8 bWAR )

Shohei Ohtani, Los Angeles Dodgers (.275/.377/.512, 30 HR, 81 RBI, 11 SB; 85.2 IP, 1.79 ERA, 2.61 FIP, 0.95 WHIP, 10.0 K/9, 6.5 bWAR )

Brice Turang, Milwaukee Brewers (.268/.366/.450, 21 HR, 100 RBI, 19 SB, 7.3 bWAR )

Even more absurd than Crow-Armstrong's historic 40/40 campaign is the fact that we spent the first two months of it wondering if he was OK.

Through 58 games, PCA was making minimal impact on offense. We're talking a .676 OPS with six home runs and 12 stolen bases. Seattle's Josh Naylor was simultaneously sitting at .676, five and 12, respectively, and goodness knows we spent the entire season questioning what happened to him.

From May 30 through to the end of the regular season, however, PCA played out of his mind, posting a 1.076 OPS with 39 home runs and 29 stolen bases—162-game paces of 60.8 and 45.2, respectively.

While also playing sensational defense in center field, we might add. He was officially awarded the Platinum Glove for most valuable defender in the National League on Friday.

FanGraphs tabulated his impact for those 104 games at a 9.1 WAR . The next-closest player was Fernando Tatis Jr. at a 4.9.

While that was going on, the early favorite for NL MVP vanished.

Through 90 games, a fifth MVP for Ohtani looked inevitable, and a first Cy Young award looked plausible. But thanks to the combination of a left knee injury and a right biceps injury, he stopped pitching in early July and stopped producing at the plate in mid-August.

By late August, PCA was already starting to look like the pick for NL MVP. But when he hit five home runs in the span of two games against the Reds, this race was as good as over.

articles.title: Mariners Players Involved in Search for New Manager, Latest MLB Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: The Seattle Mariners reportedly took a unique approach in their search for a new manager this offseason.
articles.body:
The Seattle Mariners reportedly took a unique approach in their search for a new manager this offseason.

The Athletic's Ken Rosenthal reported that a "select group of Mariners players, veterans who are considered clubhouse leaders, participated in the final managerial interviews" before Jason Kanzler was hired for the position last week.

As Rosenthal noted, MLB players "normally have no input in the selection of a manager." Mariners president of baseball operations Jerry Dipoto had previously declared that player input wouldn't factor into the team's decision.

"That remains to be seen. I think there's also a danger zone there, but they'll be in tune as to what we're doing, and they will give us the feedback that is required to make sure that this is a good fit. But we're not going to ask them to be a part of an interview process," Dipoto said last month .

In the end, the Mariners went with Kanzler, who previously served as the Chicago Cubs' farm director and has never managed at any level. Rosenthal reported that Seattle chose Kanzler over Joe Espada, who managed the Houston Astros for three seasons before being fired last month.

Despite Kanzler taking over as manager, the Mariners retained multiple coaches from the previous regime, including pitching coach Pete Woodworth and director of pitching strategy Trent Blank. CJ Gillman, their minor-league coordinator from 2022 to 2025, was hired as their pitching coach, and former New York Yankees catching instructor Tanner Swanson was hired as their bench coach.

Kanzler and company will be tasked with turning around a Mariners franchise that has missed the playoffs in three of the last four years.

articles.title: New Tarik Skubal Rumors on Cubs' Pursuit amid Dodgers, Mets Buzz Entering MLB Free Agency
articles.summary: The Chicago Cubs have no plans to enter the Tarik Skubal sweepstakes, according to The Athletic's Sahadev Sharma.
articles.body:
The Chicago Cubs have no plans to enter the Tarik Skubal sweepstakes, according to The Athletic's Sahadev Sharma .

"The Cubs have shown no interest in spending like the Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Mets," Sharma reported. "This winter, one in which labor negotiations muddy the waters for teams and their finances, won't be an exception."

To that end, Chicago won't be willing to meet the cost it will take to sign Skubal, though it "will at least check in on every other free-agent pitcher."

The New York Post 's Jon Heyman reported last week the Dodgers and Mets are shaping up to be the most aggressive suitors for the two-time Cy Young Award winner.

For Cubs fans, ownership's investment has been a regular source of frustration in recent years. The 2020 season is the last time Chicago had a top-five payroll on Opening Day.

One can question the ultimate value in paying a pitcher at the top end of the market. Peruse the list of highest-paid aces and there are a lot of starters who have battled injuries, haven't performed well, or suffered from a combination of the two.

Nobody will argue over Skubal's dominance on the mound. Since the start of 2023, he has posted a 2.47 ERA and 2.42 FIP while averaging 10.9 strikeouts per nine innings. He's one of the best in the game and by far the best starting pitcher in free agency this winter.

Still, there's always some risk in shelling out for a starter who's about to enter his age-30 season, especially for the money Skubal will command. ESPN's Kiley McDaniel projected the southpaw to get $352 million over eight years.

In time, the Cubs might be vindicated if they make little to no effort to sign Skubal.

But it always sends a bad message with a team preemptively removes itself from the running for a marquee free agent. There's also the fact that shopping in the lower tiers of the market often means you get what you pay for.

The Cubs struck gold when they bought low on Jake Arrieta, but their general approach to pitching has far more often yielded good but not great solutions like Jameson Taillon, Matthew Boyd, Drew Smyly and Marcus Stroman.

Once again, the front office might ultimately fail to improve the starting rotation to a meaningful degree if it has to set its ceiling at Freddy Peralta, Michael King or Trevor Rogers.

articles.title: MLB MVP 2026 Odds and Predictions for Yordan Alvarez, Pete Crow-Armstrong, More
articles.summary: The 2026 MLB playoffs ended on October 29, when the Milwaukee Brewers finished off the Tampa Bay Rays in a five-game World Series to claim the title. This week, Major League Baseball will reflect on the season that was, handing out awards to the biggest stars of the year.
articles.body:
The 2026 MLB playoffs ended on October 29, when the Milwaukee Brewers finished off the Tampa Bay Rays in a five-game World Series to claim the title. This week, Major League Baseball will reflect on the season that was, handing out awards to the biggest stars of the year.

The first awards were handed out on Saturday, and the week will culminate with the announcement of the AL and NL MVPs on Thursday, November 12.

Updates and award winners can be found at MLB.com throughout the week.

Here, we'll examine the MVP races, the top finalists, and why Yordan Alvarez and Pete Crow-Armstrong have been heavy favorites since the end of the regular season.

FanDuel has since removed its MVP odds, but we'll also look at the odds from the end of the season.

Yordan Alvarez, DH, Houston Astros -20000 (bet $20,000 to win $100)

Junior Caminero, 3B, Tampa Bay Rays +1200 (bet $100 to win $1,200

Pete Crow-Armstrong, CF, Chicago Cubs -1500

Shohei Ohtani, SP/DH, Los Angeles Dodgers +750

Finalists per MLB.com . Odds from FanDuel (h/t Fox Sports ) as of September 19

One thing we know for certain is that the American League will have a new MVP in 2026. Two-time defending champion Aaron Judge has reigned over the past two seasons, but the New York Yankees star battled injuries throughout the year and fell out of the mix.

Bobby Witt, who was an AL MVP finalist in 2024, wasn't as impressive as he was a couple of years ago. However, the Kansas City Royals standout played strong defense while logging 157 hits, 54 RBI, 18 home runs, and a .281 batting average.

However, Witt didn't impress enough to be considered a betting favorite at the end of the season. Neither did Junior Caminero, though the Tampa Bay Rays infielder was at least on the board.

Caminero played all 162 regular-season games and finished with 170 hits, 101 RBI, and 42 home runs. He was also solid in Tampa's run to the World Series, though the MVP is supposed to be a regular-season award.

Of course, there's no real mystery in the AL race. Yordan Alvarez has been the star of the show and was a very heavy favorite before the end of the regular season.

The Houston Astros' star DH was simply fantastic from the beginning of the year to the end. He finished as the league-leader in batting average (.316), on-base percentage (.432), slugging percentage (.601), and total bases (341). He also hit 106 RBI and 42 home runs.

Things aren't quite as settled in the National League, and there's at least a chance we could see a repeat MVP.

Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher and designated hitter Shohei Ohtani had an unexpected slump in the postseason but largely impressed during the regular season. Injuries limited the four-time MVP to 14 starts as a pitcher, but he notched eight wins with a 1.79 ERA.

As a batter, Ohtani delivered 144 hits, 30 home runs, and 81 RBI while batting .275 and stealing 11 bases. The 32-year-old has won three straight MVPs and is in the mix for a fourth.

Brice Turang is a first-time finalist and a true dark horse, but the Brewers' second baseman deserves recognition. He played elite defense during Milwaukee's championship run, and he delivered 21 home runs, 100 RBIs, 19 steals, and an .816 OPS.

While Pete Crow-Armstrong isn't as heavy of a favorite as Alvarez, though, he's still quite likely to be crowned MVP. The Chicago Cubs outfielder was sensational throughout the season.

Crow-Armstrong racked up 45 home runs and 41 stolen bases, making him just the seventh member of the fabled 40-40 club. He added 175 hits and 107 RBI while batting .280 and playing excellent Gold Glove defense at center field. He played an unquestionably large role in putting Chicago in the postseason.

"It's about as raw and straightforward as it gets," shortstop Dansby Swanson said, per ESPN's Jesse Rodgers . "With him and without him, what would we be?"

Ohtani's two-way prowess could allow him to earn the upset, but the prediction here is that PCA will be your 2026 NL MVP.

articles.title: Latest MLB Free Agents 2026 Rumors, Predictions for Tarik Skubal, Teruaki Sato, More
articles.summary: The Tarik Skubal sweepstakes is officially open and the hard-throwing lefty may put pen to paper sooner than expected.
articles.body:
The Tarik Skubal sweepstakes is officially open and the hard-throwing lefty may put pen to paper sooner than expected.

The two-time Cy Young Award winner's plans for the offseason are the headline topic of this collection of insider reports, which also includes the latest on international sensation Teruaki Sato and a former Gold Glove winner coming off a strong season and attracting plenty of attention.

Latest on Tarik Skubal's Contract Timeline

Jon Heyman of the New York Post reported that Tarik Skubal is likely to sign in November, before the collective bargaining agreement runs out in December (h/t CBS Sports ).

He added that there is no deal imminent, but the market is moving for the 30-year-old southpaw.

Skubal is coming off another strong year that saw him go 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA, 186 strikeouts, and a 0.964 WHIP with the Tigers and Dodgers.

His numbers dipped slightly from his stellar back-to-back Cy Young Award-winning seasons, but there is little denying that he is still elite on the mound, enough so that he is likely to get a record deal when he puts pen to paper.

The Dodgers' president of baseball operations, Andrew Friedman, said at the end of the team's season, "We have a tremendous amount of respect for him on and off the field, and for us, he's put himself in this position to go out and be a free agent. And for us, it's to continue to talk to Scott [Boras, his agent]."

Clearly, the team would love to have him back on a long-term deal, as they look to build on their championship dynasty, which they fell short of adding to in 2026.

Heyman noted in his report that the New York Mets are interested in acquiring Skubal but added that the team's bidding for Juan Soto two years ago may impact how much they are willing to bid.

There will be enormous offers sent Skubal's way, and it will ultimately come down to fit and preference. The Dodgers are still a win-now team, with the pieces in place to return to the Fall Classic next year and compete for a third title in four years.

The Mets have flashed some seriously talented young stars in Nolan McLean, AJ Ewing, and Carson Benge. Whether he wants to play for the here and now, or future success could be the difference.

Prediction: Skubal signs with New York or Los Angeles, with few other teams positioned to pay out what they will

Which Teams Are Interested in Teruaki Sato

Teruaki Sato will have until the collective bargaining agreement ends on December 1 to sign with an MLB team or return to the Hanshin Tigers for the 2027 season.

With that said, the success of Munetaka Murakami last season, a big slugger with some admitted defensive concerns, has created interest in signing Sato sooner rather than later.

Heyman reported that the Mets, Phillies, Padres, and Yankees are all linked to the 27-year-old third baseman.

Sato hit .306 last season, with a .991 OPS, 39 home runs and 106 RBI. He tallied 165 total hits, the most of his career.

He accumulated a better fielding percentage as an outfielder (.944) than as a third baseman (.937), and could prove valuable to a team looking for versatility on the diamond. There are some concerns about his ability to play consistent defense, but his bat makes up for it.

It is no surprise that the four teams Heyman mentioned are interested in adding Sato given their struggles at the plate in the postseason (Phillies, Padres, and Yankees) or throughout all of 2026 (Mets).

Prediction: Sato signs before the collective bargaining agreement ends, but do not be shocked if a surprise team comes from out of nowhere to win the sweepstakes.

Ty France is drawing considerable interest from teams following a strong 2026.
